source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The Whipple procedure for pancreatic cancer removes the head of the pancreas plus:
questions.rationale: Pancreaticoduodenectomy removes the pancreatic head, gallbladder, common bile duct, and part of the duodenum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pancreatic Cancer Surgery (PDF p. 292)
questions.quote: Removal of the gallbladder, common bile duct, part of the duodenum and head of the pancreas

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a major risk factor for hepatocellular cancer in the Philippines?
questions.rationale: Risks include hepatitis B, cirrhosis, aflatoxin (moldy peanuts or corn), and alcohol.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatocellular Cancer (PDF p. 292)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Aflatoxin, a liver carcinogen, is commonly found in:
questions.rationale: Aflatoxin is produced by Aspergillus molds on improperly stored peanuts and grains.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hepatocellular Cancer (PDF p. 292)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cholecystectomy, which position promotes comfort and breathing?
questions.rationale: Low-Fowler's position, with splinting, deep breathing, and coughing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gallbladder Surgery (PDF p. 293)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has a T-tube after common bile duct exploration. Which finding should be reported?
questions.rationale: Report sudden increases in drainage, jaundice, clay stools, or dark urine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, T-tube Care (PDF p. 293)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When the T-tube is clamped before meals, the client develops nausea. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Clamp before meals as ordered; unclamp if nausea or vomiting develops.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, T-tube Care (PDF p. 293)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most common presenting symptom of colorectal cancer?
questions.rationale: Change in bowel habits is most common; blood in stools is second.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colorectal Cancer (PDF p. 293)
questions.quote: Changes in bowel habits (most common presenting symptom)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diet increases colorectal cancer risk?
questions.rationale: High-fat, high-protein, low-fiber diets are risk factors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colorectal Cancer (PDF p. 293)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which tumor marker monitors colorectal cancer recurrence?
questions.rationale: Carcinoembryonic antigen is used for colorectal cancer.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colorectal Diagnosis (PDF p. 294)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is neomycin given before bowel surgery?
questions.rationale: Oral neomycin, plus bowel cleansing and low-residue diet, reduces infection risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pre-operative Interventions (PDF p. 294)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Removal of the tumor, sigmoid, rectum, and anal sphincter (Miles procedure) results in:
questions.rationale: Abdominoperineal resection removes the rectum and sphincter, requiring a permanent colostomy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colorectal Surgery (PDF p. 294)
questions.quote: Removal of the tumor and a portion of the sigmoid and all of the rectum and anal sphincter

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A new colostomy stoma appears dark and dusky. This indicates:
questions.rationale: A normal stoma is red and moist; dusky, brown, or black suggests necrosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stoma Care (PDF p. 294)
questions.quote: Abnormal: Dark, dusky brown — black; these suggest

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should a colostomy pouch be emptied?
questions.rationale: Empty at 1/3 to 1/2 full to prevent leakage and pouch separation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stoma Care (PDF p. 294)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The client feels cramping during colostomy irrigation. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Stop momentarily when cramps occur, then continue slowly; the bag hangs 12–18 inches above the stoma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Irrigation (PDF p. 294)
questions.quote: Stop irrigation momentarily when cramps are felt; continue the irrigation slowly

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How high should the colostomy irrigation bag be hung above the stoma?
questions.rationale: Hang 12–18 inches above the stoma and insert the lubricated catheter 2–4 inches.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Irrigation (PDF p. 294)
questions.quote: Hang solution 12-18 inches above the stoma

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which food should a client with a colostomy limit to reduce gas?
questions.rationale: Avoid gas-forming foods: cabbage, cauliflower, nuts, carbonated drinks, gum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Colostomy Diet (PDF p. 295)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the earliest and most common sign of bladder cancer?
questions.rationale: Painless hematuria is the earliest and most common sign.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bladder Cancer (PDF p. 295)
questions.quote: Painless hematuria (earliest and most common sign)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the strongest risk factor for bladder cancer?
questions.rationale: Smoking and industrial carcinogen exposure are leading risks; men are affected more.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bladder Cancer (PDF p. 295)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In an ileal conduit, urine drains through a stoma made from:
questions.rationale: An ileal conduit uses a segment of ileum as the stoma for urine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bladder Cancer Surgery (PDF p. 295)
questions.quote: Ileal Conduit Ileum used as stoma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which skin cancer is most common and rarely metastasizes?
questions.rationale: Basal cell carcinoma is most common with good prognosis; melanoma is deadliest.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Cancer (PDF p. 295)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which mole feature should prompt evaluation for melanoma?
questions.rationale: ABCDE: asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter > 6 mm, elevation or evolution.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Cancer Parameters (PDF p. 296)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which person has the highest risk for skin cancer?
questions.rationale: Fair skin, sunburns, and chronic sun exposure are major risks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Cancer Risk Factors (PDF p. 296)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the hallmark sign of iron deficiency anemia?
questions.rationale: Fatigue is the hallmark; also spoon nails, pallor, pica, and angular cheilosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Iron Deficiency Anemia (PDF p. 297)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Spoon-shaped nails seen in iron deficiency anemia are called:
questions.rationale: Koilonychia is spoon-shaped nails from iron deficiency.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Iron Deficiency Anemia (PDF p. 297)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a client take ferrous sulfate tablets for best absorption?
questions.rationale: Vitamin C increases iron absorption; dairy and antacids decrease it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Iron Therapy (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Taken with Vit C to increase absorption

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on oral iron reports black stools. The nurse explains:
questions.rationale: Black stools are a common, expected effect of oral iron.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Iron Therapy (PDF p. 298)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which technique is used for IM iron dextran injection?
questions.rationale: Z-track prevents leakage and skin staining; do not massage the site.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parenteral Iron (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Administer using Z-tract method to prevent discoloration and leakage to tissues

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the pathognomonic sign of pernicious anemia?
questions.rationale: Red beefy tongue (glossitis) with paresthesias and loss of proprioception.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pernicious Anemia (PDF p. 298)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test diagnoses vitamin B12 malabsorption in pernicious anemia?
questions.rationale: Schilling test: radioactive B12 is given and a 24-hour urine is collected.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pernicious Anemia (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Schilling's test for absorption of vitamin B12

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with pernicious anemia asks how long B12 injections are needed. The nurse says:
questions.rationale: Without intrinsic factor, B12 injections are given monthly for life.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pernicious Anemia (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: Administer Vit. B12 injections at monthly intervals for lifetime as ordered.
